0-4834-16-t.subevent: Demonstrators in Baghdad and mainly in Sadr City took to the streets on Thursday in denunciation of lack of services, unemployment and unfair apportionment.
Public sector employees joined residents in their rally.
Oil Ministry employees called to be included in the staffing cadre just as their mates in other ministries.
Employees of the General groups firm related to the Ministry of Industry and minerals protested against the decision to cut off 20% of their salaries.
All Iraqis are united over the call to improve their situation, ascertain security in the country and boost its economy.

33-2389-1-1.subevent: YouTube announced it is removing videos that push extremist views like white supremacy or deny events like the Holocaust or Sandy Hook shooting.

The new policy prohibits any video alleging that a group is superior to justify discrimination, segregation, or exclusion based on qualities like age, gender, race, caste, religion, sexual orientation, or veteran status.
YouTube did not specify which channels or videos it is removing.
The update follows a controversy when YouTube refused to take down the channel of conservative personality Stephen Crowder for using homophobic slurs against journalist Carlos Maza.
YouTube initially said Crowder's videos didn't violate the site's rules, stating that opinions can be deeply offensive but if they don't violate policies, they remain on the site.
YouTube announced it would remove channels that 'brush up' against its hate speech rules from its YouTube Partner Program.
For other 'borderline' content, YouTube said it would reduce the reach of the video and surround it with more authoritative content.
YouTube later said it would suspend monetization on Crowder's channel.
YouTube said Crowder would be able to monetize his channel again if he addressed certain issues, including removing a link from the video selling his T-shirts and merchandise.
The new hate speech policy comes as platforms like YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter face intense scrutiny for their content policing abilities.
YouTube said it has partnered with lawmakers and other organizations to help combat the spread of extremism on its service.
The Anti-Defamation League applauded the new policy but called on YouTube to do more.

0-4488-1-1.subevent: On Feb. 1, Boko Haram launched its second attack on Maiduguri, but Nigerian troops beat back the attackers.
Boko Haram captured Baga and surrounding villages at the beginning of the year, and later captured Monguno after a foiled attack on Maiduguri.
Reliable estimates of Boko Haram's strength do not exist, with experts putting the number between 5,000 and 50,000.
Boko Haram has transformed into a territorial insurgency comparable to Al Shabaab and the Islamic State.
At its peak, Islamic State had about 31,500 fighters, now about 25,000, while Al Shabaab fields about 5,000 well-trained militants.
Boko Haram controls an area the size of Belgium, and its core strength is estimated at 7,000 to 10,000 fighters.
Boko Haram has an additional reserve of several thousand novice recruits and slave soldiers, possibly adding 10,000 auxiliaries from recruitment and abductions.
The core strength fits Boko Haram's tactical profile, as it can defeat hundreds but falters against thousands.
Nigeria, Cameroon, and Chad have deployed about 35,000 troops against Boko Haram, and if Chadians operate in Nigeria with air support, they might block advances.
Insurgencies rely on terrain and local support, and Boko Haram has both, similar to Al Shabaab which has held out despite disadvantages.
Little is known about Boko Haram's financial and organizational capabilities, unlike Islamic State and Al Shabaab.

1-14826-2-13.subevent: Alicia Soto attended the 1 October Sunrise Remembrance Ceremony for the third consecutive year.
Soto said that attending the ceremony helps her process her trauma and that she decided to live life to the fullest for those who died.
A slideshow displayed the names and pictures of the 58 people killed, plus two women who died within the past year from injuries.
Clark County Sheriff Joe Lombardo announced that Kimberly Gervais and Samanta Arjune would be added to the official death toll, raising it to 60.
The Review-Journal published an article that highlighted the deaths of the two women and reported the police department's initial decision not to include them.
Lombardo said in a brief interview that he was comfortable acknowledging that the two women lost their lives as a result of the shooting.
The ceremony had fewer attendees due to the coronavirus pandemic, and Governor Steve Sisolak prioritized the event when raising the gathering limit.
Sisolak said in a shaky voice that the state will never forget the event and the lives lost and changed.
Albert Rivera, father of victim Jordyn Rivera, thanked survivors for supporting each other.
Rivera acknowledged Greg Zanis, who built 58 crosses and died in May, and said his kindness changed him.
Rivera called for unity and urged people to remember how they came together after the shooting.

0-4716-1-1.subevent: The social uprising in Chile has reached its fourth month.
Masses continue to protest despite ferocious repression by the militarized Carabineros, which have not been reformed since the dictatorship.
Chileans are looking ahead to a plebiscite that may open the way to a new Constitution.
Pinochet's 1980 Constitution institutionalized the authoritarian model and neoliberal framework.
The Constitution restricted political participation and gave the Right disproportionate power.
President Piñera declared 'We are at war' and called army troops to patrol streets.
On October 25, 1.2 million people gathered to protest in Santiago's Plaza Italia.
Human rights organizations and the UN criticized security forces for excessive force and legislative initiatives.
Chile has extreme inequality, with a life expectancy gap of 18 years and income inequality 65% wider than OECD average.
The privatized pension system pays 80% of retirees less than the minimum wage.
The metro fare hike sparked the social uprising.
Congress passed an anti-looting law criminalizing protest tactics.

6-19306-4-t.subevent: The Northern Ireland economy is now highly unlikely to recover all the output lost in the last recession before the next one begins.
New official figures show that in the final quarter of 2019 the economy was still 4% smaller than its 2007 peak.
It is now facing a deep recession as a result of the ongoing coronavirus crisis.
The Ulster University Economic Policy Centre has estimated that output could fall by almost 10% in 2020.
The official figures, produced by the Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (Nisra), suggest that the economy grew by 0.7% in 2019.
That compares to GDP growth of 1.4% for the UK as a whole in the same period.
The Northern Ireland economy was already slowing before the crisis began.
Quarterly growth in the last three months of 2019 was just 0.2%, driven by the public sector and manufacturing.
The service sector, which is the dominant part of the economy, showed no growth.
Nisra said official statistical evidence of the scale of the economic crisis will only be clear when the figures for the second quarter of 2020 are compiled.
Those figures are not due to be released until October.

1-16475-1-1.subevent: An ancient gold coin described as a 'naked and shameless celebration' of Julius Caesar's assassination, featuring a portrait of Brutus, sold for a record $3.5 million.
The coin was bought by an anonymous bidder for £2.7 million ($3.5 million).
The coin features a portrait of Marcus Junius Brutus, one of the ringleaders in Caesar's assassination.
The coin also depicts the daggers used by Brutus and Cassius and a cap of Liberty.
The coin is inscribed with 'Eid Mar' (Ides of March), the date of Caesar's death.
The coin was issued by Brutus two years after the assassination, in 42 BC.
Richard Beale, managing director of Roma Numismatics, described the coin as a 'naked and shameless celebration' of the assassination.
Caesar's death was fueled by the belief among Roman politicians that he intended to make himself king.
Caesar was killed by a group of senators, including friends and people he had pardoned, after being appointed dictator for life.
Brutus killed himself after losing the Battle of Philippi to Octavius and Mark Antony.
Despite its age, the coin is in near-mint condition and is one of only three known to exist.
The previous record price for a Roman coin was set in 2008 when a bronze sestertius sold for $2.5 million; the previous record for any coin was $3.25 million in 2012.

0-4450-1-2.subevent: Authorities said at least 13 people died and several others were missing after a migrant ship sank off the Italian island of Lampedusa.
The boat overturned shortly after midnight.
Rescuers pulled the bodies of 13 women, some pregnant, from the water on Monday.
The ship had roughly 50 people on board; 22 survivors were rescued.
Among those still missing are eight children and other pregnant women.
The vessel capsized as rescue boats approached due to adverse weather and passengers rushing to one side.
Authorities described the ship as an overloaded and listing boat six nautical miles from Lampedusa.
The International Organization for Migration said the boat started in Tunisia and carried predominantly Tunisians and western African migrants.

1-14826-2-14.subevent: Alicia Soto attended the 1 October Sunrise Remembrance Ceremony for the third year.
A slideshow during the ceremony displayed the names and pictures of the 58 people killed in the shooting.

The slideshow included pictures of two women who died within the past year from injuries suffered in the mass shooting, with a message reading 'In Memoriam of 1 October Victims Lost in the Last Year.'
Clark County Sheriff Joe Lombardo announced that Kimberly Gervais and Samanta Arjune would be added to the official death toll, raising the number from 58 to 60.
Lombardo said that the announcement came after the Review-Journal published an article on Monday about their deaths and the police department's initial decision not to include them.
Lombardo stated in an interview that he is comfortable acknowledging the two individuals lost their lives as a result of 1 October.
The ceremony had fewer attendees due to the coronavirus pandemic, which forced officials to limit attendance.
Gov. Steve Sisolak said that raising the limit on public gatherings for Thursday's event was one of his biggest priorities.
Sisolak's voice grew shaky as he recalled the night and offered condolences to the family members of those who died.
Sisolak said, 'We will never, never forget what happened that day, or the lives that were lost, and the lives that were changed.'
Albert Rivera, father of victim Jordyn Rivera, thanked survivors who continue to come together on the anniversary and support each other.
Rivera said, 'We are all a statistic — we are all part of this unwanted fraternity we didn’t chose to be a part of.'
Rivera acknowledged Greg Zanis, who built 58 crosses honoring the victims and died in May of bladder cancer, and said he will be forever changed by Zanis' kindness.
Rivera called for unity during a time of divisiveness and urged people to remember how they came together on Oct. 2, 2017.
Rivera ended his remarks by saying, 'It’s said that it takes more effort to hate than to love. Let’s remember that. Until we meet again — here, there or in the air — may we all smile like Jordyn.'

0-4388-1-1.subevent: A new report claims 13 million Italians live in areas where the mafia exerts influence over everyday life.
The report was commissioned by Italy's parliamentary anti-mafia commission and conducted by research institute Censis using crime statistics.
The report stated that Italians in the 610 identified districts are conditioned by the mafia's capillary control in the area.
Giuseppe Pisanu, head of the anti-mafia commission, said the Italian mafia is now moving from spectacular crimes to business and politics.
Censis found the highest concentration of people living under the shadow of the mafia was 95.9% in Agrigento, Sicily, followed by Naples at 95%.
The four main Italian mafia groups have an estimated annual turnover of €130bn.
Pisanu pointed out that the 22% of Italians living under the mob's shadow produce just 14.6% of Italy's GDP and hold 12.4% of bank deposits.
In Catania and Palermo, 80% of shops allegedly pay protection money starting from €500 a month.
Suspicious fires in the four regions studied by Censis doubled to 8,441 per year between 1998 and 2007.
Investigators believe Italy's clans are now investing profits from extortion and drug dealing outside the Italian south, including in building work for Milan's Expo 2015.
The Camorra and 'Ndrangheta are suspected of investing in Rome, with the Camorra focusing on suburban shopping centres and the 'Ndrangheta on luxury property and restaurants.
Pisanu said the mafias are also investing overseas, and the 'Ndrangheta has offered to act as a financial services consultant to Colombian cartels.

3-17632-4-t.subevent: Women and Family Minister Datuk Seri Rina Harun visited the monitoring centre in Nilai on Saturday (March 21).
Rina Harun expressed satisfaction with preparations at the centre to receive 55 returnees from Iran on Sunday (March 22).
Rina Harun stated that the centre will house the returnees, who are expected to arrive at 10.30am, and will also place 23 officers involved in the mission and crew members.
Rina Harun said there were 46 Malaysians, eight Singaporeans, and one Indonesian among the returnees.
Rina Harun said the Social Welfare Department would work with other agencies to take care of those at the monitoring centre, including preparing food and providing counselling.
Rina Harun said they would adopt the same standard operating procedure as the previous mission.
The government is bringing home 46 Malaysians stranded in Iran on a special flight scheduled to land at Kuala Lumpur International Airport 2 at 6.10am Sunday.
Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Kamarudin Jaffar said the AirAsia flight departed Tehran at 11.45 am Saturday.

2-34597-1-1.subevent: The Lucy mission launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 5:34 a.m. ET on Saturday morning.
The launch team confirmed a signal from the spacecraft and that it was safe and healthy, with solar arrays deployed.
Lucy will embark on a 12-year mission to explore Jupiter's Trojan asteroids, which have never been observed.
The Trojan asteroids orbit the sun in two swarms, one ahead of and one behind Jupiter.
Lucy will provide the first high-resolution images of the Trojan asteroids.
The asteroids are remnants from the early solar system and will help researchers learn how the solar system formed.
NASA's Thomas Zurbuchen said the mission is important because the asteroids tell about the history of the outer planets' formation.
The spacecraft will fly by an asteroid in the main belt and then explore seven Trojan asteroids, using three gravity assists from Earth.
The mission is named after the Lucy fossil, and the logo includes a diamond from the Beatles song.
Lucy will travel nearly 4 billion miles over 12 years, visiting asteroids named from Homer's 'The Iliad'.
The spacecraft has large solar panels and is NASA's first mission far from the sun without nuclear power.
After the mission, the team plans an extended mission; the spacecraft will remain in a stable orbit for over 100,000 years.

0-4448-1-1.subevent: An UAA Ukraine Air Alliance Antonov AN-12 freighter on approach to Lviv disappeared from radar and was found on the ground after an emergency landing due to fuel exhaustion.
Five occupants were killed, three were taken to hospital with injuries.
Ukraine's State Emergency Services reported the aircraft disappeared from radar at 07:10L, and at 07:29L a crew member called reporting an emergency landing.
At 07:40L the aircraft was located 1.5km before the runway.
Three bodies were found, three injured were taken to hospital, two were missing and later found dead.
The Mayor of Lviv reported the crew declared emergency due to low fuel but did not reach the runway.
The aircraft was found with the cockpit cut off and cargo shifted.
Ukraine's NBAAI reported the aircraft was scheduled to refuel at Lviv, and the emergency landing resulted in a disaster about 1.5km before runway 31.
On Oct 5th 2019, the European Aviation Safety Agency revoked the airline's authorized third country operator status.
On Oct 7th 2019, Ukraine's Ministry of Transport terminated the airline's air operator's certificate effective Oct 5th 2019.
On Oct 9th 2019, the NBAAI announced a special commission was formed, the black boxes were recovered and read out, and information from ground facilities was collected.
On Dec 20th 2019, the NBAAI released their preliminary report.
The FDR and CVR were found in satisfactory condition and read out; the crew did not provide critical remarks up to intercepting the localizer.
At 03:40:01 UTC, the crew reported capturing the Runway-31 localizer beam.
At 03:41:58 UTC, the controller cleared landing and the crew confirmed.
At 03:43:34 UTC, at a distance of 1.67 km from the threshold, engine mode increased briefly then decreased, vertical speed was 4 m/s, height 48 m, speed 244 km/h (below manual).
At a height of about 30 m, 2-3 seconds before collision with trees, the elevator pitched up by 75% but was insufficient; the aircraft continued descending and collided with trees.
During the flight along the glide path, none of the crew members reported the aircraft's position relative to the glide path.
Analysis showed the crew increased speed three times by increasing vertical speed, indicating inadequate actions of the PIC.
Inspection of the accident site found the glide slope and heading alarm flags were turned off.

1-wiki-img/15491-1/15491-1-2.subevent: Mars will be at its biggest and brightest in the night sky as it lines up with Earth on the same side of the sun.
The event, known as opposition, occurs when Mars and the sun are on directly opposite sides of Earth.
All three bodies will be in a straight line at roughly 11:30pm.
Mars will be at its best around 1am on Wednesday, according to the Royal Observatory Greenwich.
Astronomer Hannah Banyard said that the last opposition in 2018 was difficult to see, but this time it is a good chance.
She added that for about a month, Mars has been easy to see as it rises earlier and gets high in the sky.
NASA described opposition as when Mars and the sun are on opposite sides of Earth, with Mars rising at sunset and setting at sunrise.
Despite cloudy weather forecasts, Mars should be visible through any breaks or lighter cloud.
Ms. Banyard said Mars can be seen with the naked eye, but recommended a four-inch telescope with 24-millimetre magnification.
To the naked eye, Mars looks like a blurry orange star; with a telescope, some surface features are visible.
The next time Mars will be this big and bright will be 2033.

2-34752-6-1.subevent: Toxic blue-green algae thrive in warm, slow-moving water.
Harmful algae usually bloom during the warm summer season or when water temperatures are warmer than usual.
Toxic blue-green algae prefer warmer water.
Warmer temperatures prevent water from mixing, allowing algae to grow thicker and faster.
Warmer water is easier for small organisms to move through and allows algae to float to the surface faster.
Algal blooms absorb sunlight, making water even warmer and promoting more blooms.
Climate change might lead to more droughts, making freshwater saltier, which can cause marine algae to invade freshwater ecosystems.
In the southwestern and south central United States, toxic marine algae have been killing fish in freshwater lakes since 2000.
Higher levels of carbon dioxide in the air and water can lead to rapid growth of algae, especially toxic blue-green algae.
Climate change might affect rainfall patterns, leading to alternating droughts and intense storms, which cause more nutrient runoff and feed more algal blooms.
Scientists predict sea level could rise up to one meter by 2100, creating more shallow and stable coastal water perfect for algae growth.
Climate change is expected to alter the timing and intensity of coastal upwelling, and along the west coast of the United States, excess nutrients from upwelling might lead to more algal blooms.

6-wiki-img/18504-2/18504-2-1.subevent: The Chang'e-5 orbiter delivered a return module containing 1.731 kilograms of lunar samples to Earth on Dec. 16.
The orbiter then fired its engines to deep space for an extended mission.
The Chang'e-5 orbiter successfully entered an intended orbit around Sun-Earth Lagrange point 1 in March.
There it carried out tests related to orbit control and observations of the Earth and Sun.
New data from satellite trackers suggests Chang'e-5 left its orbit around Sun-Earth L1 and is destined for a lunar flyby early September 9 Eastern time.
It was noted that Chang'e-5 may have altered its orbit Aug. 30 based on observations by amateur satellite trackers and an astronomy software developer.
The spacecraft is under the control of the Beijing Aerospace Flight Control Center (BACC), which has not yet provided an update on the plans for Chang'e-5.
Potential maneuvers such as entering lunar orbit, heading for another Sun-Earth Lagrange point, or an Earth-moon Lagrange point depend on remaining propellant.
Another possibility is using the flyby to set Chang'e-5 on a trajectory to flyby 469219 Kamoʻoalewa, a quasi-satellite of Earth.
Jing Peng, deputy chief designer, said a visit to a planetary body such as Venus may not be possible due to a lack of propellant.
Jing Peng said the orbiter will likely stay at Lagrange point 1 or the Earth-moon system.
Samples collected by the Chang'e-5 lander are now being analyzed, and applications for sample materials are open to domestic and international institutions.
NASA currently has no plans to trade any of its Apollo-era lunar samples with those returned by Chang'e-5, but its chief scientist expressed hope for such an exchange in the future.

China is planning a followup lunar sample-return, Chang'e-6, in 2024, which is part of the joint China-Russia International Lunar Research Station, and the French space agency will contribute a science payload.

China's Lunar and Planetary Data System provided an update on the ongoing Chang'e-4 lunar far side mission, reporting that the Yutu-2 rover has covered roughly 799 meters across 33 lunar days since landing in January 2019.

23-13614-13-t.subevent: For over a year, Israel has allowed little more than basic humanitarian aid into Gaza to isolate Hamas and stop rocket fire.
A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas two months ago was meant to ease restrictions, but progress has been slow and frustration rising.
Raw sewage sprays out of leaks in a Gaza sewage pumping station.
Engineer Maher al-Najjar says it took months of negotiations to get Israel to allow some spare parts, and modernization is needed but Israel won't allow machinery.
Most of Gaza's sewage cannot be treated properly, so tons of raw waste flow into the sea.
Najjar says the sewage affects the port, fishermen, fish, and swimmers.
Fisherman Abdullah, 27, fishes despite health risks because there are no jobs.
Since the ceasefire, fighting has died down but strict sanctions remain.
Most of Gaza's 1.5 million people are reliant on food aid and unable to enter or leave.
Tens of thousands have lost jobs, and most industrial operations have stopped.
The Pepsi plant manager Ahmed Yazji says it's difficult to get ingredients and production has been cut drastically.
Yazji thought things would improve with the ceasefire but nothing changed.
Local economists say it will take years to recover even if freedom of movement were granted.
Some things have improved since the truce: more fuel and limited products are being allowed in.
The UN says the low volume of goods has not significantly improved living conditions.
The Israeli government says it intends to carry out commitments but wants to be sure Hamas stops rocket fire.
Hamas has reduced attacks but some rockets are still fired.
Israel has curtailed airstrikes, but inter-factional fighting among Palestinians continues.
Shifa Hospital previously received dead and injured from Israeli operations, but that is no longer the case.
People worry that unless sanctions are lifted, frustration will rise and the truce may collapse.

0-4716-3-1.subevent: Protests against high living costs and inequality grip Chile for nearly two weeks.
Protesters call for President Sebastian Pinera to step down.
The state of emergency is lifted but protests continue with clashes between police and protesters.
Police use tear gas, water cannon, rubber bullets, and pellets, prompting allegations of rights abuses.
Looting occurs and supermarkets and petrol stations are set on fire.
At least 20 civilians are killed in the unrest.
The majority of protesters are peaceful, using cacerolazo (banging spoons on pots).
Protests begin as a student-led demonstration against a metro fare rise of 30 pesos.
Economy Minister Juan Andres Fontaine says those upset can wake up earlier to pay a lower rate, causing outrage.
Students conduct mass fare evasion and destroy metro turnstiles.
Police attempt to stop students with force, and protests spill into the streets.
Metro stations, supermarkets, and petrol stations are burned, leading President Pinera to declare a state of emergency.
Pinera declares a state of emergency, suspending freedoms, deploying the military, and enforcing curfews.
Many criticize Pinera for declaring the state of emergency quickly without addressing the public.
Pinera justifies the decision by saying he wants to maintain public order against vandals.
After a mass protest of over one million people, Pinera says 'We are all listening and understanding.'
Pinera lifts the state of emergency on Sunday.
Pinera replaces eight cabinet members, including the economy minister and Interior Minister Andres Chadwick.
Unpopular education, health, and transport ministers are kept; new ministers are criticized for having little experience.
Pinera proposes social reforms including a minimum wage rise, state pension increase, and electricity cost stabilization.
Some welcome the reforms but others say they do not go far enough.
Pinera backs out of hosting the APEC trade summit and COP25 climate change summit.

1-15327-3-t.subevent: On 12 March, a salesman arriving from Dubai was found sick, tested for coronavirus, and sent home to Chengala village.
Local health officials isolated him; his test came back positive six days later, and he later recovered.
Chengala village council, led by Shahina Saleem, prepared early, opening a community kitchen and providing free lunches to over 1,200 people.
The council used helplines and WhatsApp to arrange accommodation for those needing isolation space; all quarantined for 28 days.
Over the last month, Chengala reported 22 cases and quarantined over 400 people; 20 patients recovered.
Kerala has reported only 3 deaths and over 370 confirmed cases, with over 100,000 in isolation, despite being an early hotspot.
Kerala imposed a lockdown a day before the national lockdown, conducted rigorous contact tracing, and set up care centres.
Health workers supported vulnerable groups and counsellors made 340,000 calls to counsel personnel.
Testing was limited to federal protocols, but experts credit Kerala's robust public health system and effective village councils.
The state's decentralized health care and strong grassroots democracy enabled community outreach and mass quarantine.
Officials warn that reports of flattening the curve are premature; testing has been limited, and the state got lucky with a younger infected population.
Dr. Sreejith N Kumar described the current achievement as a 'quarter-final' victory, with further challenges like the monsoon season ahead.

0-4398-1-2.subevent: Ecuador's government declared a state of emergency after protesters opposed to a fuel price hike disrupted transport nationwide.
President Lenin Moreno said he imposed the measure to 'ensure citizens' security and avoid chaos'.
Protesters were angered by Moreno's decision to end 40-year-old subsidies for fuel.
Diesel and petrol prices are expected to more than double as a result.
On Thursday, students and the transport sector led a national strike, with taxi, bus, and truck drivers blocking roads and bridges in Quito and Guayaquil.
Some protesters clashed with police, who fired tear gas; Interior Minister Maria Paula Romo said 19 people had been arrested.
Some protesters burned tyres and threw objects at armoured police vans, drawing criticism from Moreno.
Moreno said he would not allow protesters to 'impose chaos' and under the emergency measure, his government can restrict freedoms and deploy the armed forces.
The elimination of fuel subsidies is part of Moreno's plan to shore up Ecuador's economy and ease its debt burden, and the government agreed to cut public spending as part of an IMF loan deal.
Ecuador announced it was leaving OPEC to pump more oil and raise revenue.

24-31161-1-t.subevent: Transgender weightlifter Laurel Hubbard competed at the Tokyo Olympics on Monday night in the women's over-87-kilogram division.
Hubbard couldn't complete any of her first three lifts, ruling her out of medal contention.
The division was won by China's Li Wenwen.
Hubbard made a heart gesture to the audience with her hands before leaving the competition arena.
Hubbard thanked the IOC, the International Weightlifting Federation, and the people of Japan in a statement after exiting the competition.
Hubbard received applause and applauded her fellow athletes when they were introduced on stage.
Hubbard overbalanced on her opening weight of 120 kilograms, taking the bar behind her shoulders.
Hubbard's second effort of 125 kilograms was ruled invalid on a majority decision by the referees.
Hubbard's third attempt was almost a repeat of the first and also failed.
Athletes are eliminated if they do not record at least one valid lift in each of the two parts of the competition.
Li's victory gave China its seventh gold medal in weightlifting at the Tokyo Games.
Emily Campbell finished 37 kilograms behind Li to take silver, becoming the first British woman to win a weightlifting medal.
Sarah Robles of the United States repeated her bronze from 2016 with 282 kilograms, becoming the first U.S. woman with two weightlifting medals.
Robles commented that the referees were doing their jobs and it was very strict, which is appropriate for the Olympics.
The International Olympic Committee in 2015 drew up a set of recommendations for including transgender athletes, and many sports bodies including the IWF implemented similar policies.
In weightlifting, athletes must show their testosterone is below a certain level after transitioning, a requirement which Hubbard met.
Hubbard won a silver medal at the 2017 world championships but had not competed for 1.5 years before Tokyo due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Hubbard issued a statement saying her performance wasn't what she hoped but she was humbled by the support she received.
The IOC will release a new "framework" for transgender athletes’ eligibility in the coming months.
The New Zealand Olympic Committee acknowledged that gender identity in sport is a highly sensitive and complex issue.

0-4347-1-1.subevent: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc. is increasing the number of stores it expects to shutter in the fiscal year.
The company says it will close 60 stores in the fiscal year across the company, up 20 from the April estimate of 40 stores.
Most closings are expected after the holiday shopping season in early 2020, company officials said during a quarterly earnings call Wednesday.
Forty of the stores closing will be Bed Bath & Beyond stores and 20 will be stores in the company's other concepts, interim CEO Mary Winston said.
Winston said the 'fleet optimization' will create a better balance between physical and digital presence.
As of end of August, the company had 1,534 stores total.
Winston said there are plans to renegotiate all leases and that $350 million of inventory will be removed from stores before the 2019 holiday season through markdowns and clearance events.
According to Coresight Research, nearly 8,600 store closures have been announced so far this year in the retail sector, up from around 5,900 in 2018.
Coresight estimates closures could reach 12,000 by the end of the year.

0-4569-4-1jpg.subevent: A former Fort Worth police officer was indicted by a grand jury for murder in the death of Atatiana Jefferson, with the Tarrant County District Attorney confirming the indictment to CBS News on Friday.
Jefferson was shot and killed in October when Officer Aaron Dean fired through a window.
Dean was in the backyard of Jefferson's home when he shot Jefferson through a window after responding to a call from a neighbor about the front door being open.
Dean resigned two days after the shooting and just hours before being arrested and charged with murder.
According to Dean's arrest affidavit, Jefferson was inside a bedroom playing video games with her 8-year-old nephew moments before the shooting.
The 8-year-old boy told police his aunt heard noises outside and grabbed her handgun.
Bodycam video showed Dean walking around the home, shining a flashlight into a window and shouting 'Put your hands up! Show me your hands!' and less than a second later firing a shot.
Investigators confirmed that Dean did not identify himself as an officer at any point.
Less than three weeks after Jefferson's murder, Judge David Hagerman issued a gag order surrounding the proceedings.
The gag order prevents anyone connected with the case from making statements about witnesses, evidence or any opinion about Dean's guilt or innocence.

2-34826-6-t.subevent: Turkey recognized Kazakhstan as the first country to do so.
Many agreements and protocols were signed between Turkey and Kazakhstan after Kazakhstan's independence.
The Strategic Partnership Agreement was signed during President Nursultan Nazarbayev's visit to Turkey in October 2009.
The High Level Strategic Cooperation Council (HLSCC) was established during then Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's visit to Kazakhstan in May 2012.
The first meeting of the HLSCC was held on 11-12 October 2012 during President Nursultan Nazarbayev's visit to Turkey.
The second meeting of the HLSCC was held during President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's visit to Kazakhstan on 15-17 April 2015.
Bilateral trade volume between Turkey and Kazakhstan reached almost 3.9 billion dollars in 2019.
Turkish construction companies completed projects worth 23.5 billion dollars in Kazakhstan by 2019.
The Summit of Turkic Speaking States was institutionalized as a result of cooperation between Turkey and Kazakhstan.
Kazakhstan played a significant role in the establishment of the Turkic Council and TURKPA.
Kazakhstan hosts the International Turkic Academy.
About 8,000 students study at the campuses of International Hodja Ahmet Yesevi Turkish-Kazakh University.

12-wiki-img/8552-1/8552-1-1.subevent: Afghanistan said it would keep its main crossings with Iran open as of Monday.
Officials stated that keeping the border open allows checking returnees and quarantining those affected, while closing it would push returnees to use illegal routes, increasing contamination risk.
Faisal Javid, spokesman for President Ashraf Ghani's national security adviser, explained that the official routes are kept open to check people and separate the infected.
Javid added that if the border were sealed, people would use illegal crossings and undetected infected individuals could enter.
Officials reported that 141 people have tested positive for COVID-19 in Afghanistan, with at least four deaths in the past month.
A ministry official stated that the virus was brought by economic migrants fleeing Iran due to joblessness and the economy.

Abdul Basit Ansari, a spokesman for the Ministry of Repatriations of Refugees, reported that at least 10,000 refugees return from Iran to Afghanistan daily through the official border crossing in Herat province.
Ansari added that most returnees come voluntarily, while a few are forced to return.
Officials said closing the border is out of the question because returnees would use human traffickers via illegal routes.
Waheed Mayar, a Public Health Ministry spokesman, warned that closing the border would cause more positive cases, danger, and deaths.
The main official crossing leads to Herat province, which has become the area worst affected by COVID-19.
Javid said authorities increased preventive measures including checking all returnees and isolating those affected.
Authorities extended the lockdown in Herat by three more weeks and enforced a curfew in Kabul.
Residents, including shopkeeper Fateh Shah, expressed concern about the spread of the virus and their future.

2-34513-5-t.subevent: Lebanese Prime Minister Najib Mikati announced on Twitter that Friday would be a day of public mourning for the lives of those killed in violence in Beirut on Thursday.

Six Shi’ites were shot dead in Beirut in an attack on supporters of Hezbollah and an allied Lebanese party who were gathering to demand the removal of the judge investigating last year’s devastating Beirut port blast.

6-18755-14-1.subevent: The Madras High Court’s Madurai Bench lifted the ban on TikTok, subject to certain conditions.
The court vacated its interim order banning the app, subject to conditions that pornographic videos will not be uploaded, failing which contempt proceedings would begin.
TikTok said it was glad about the decision and believed it was welcomed by its community in India.
Earlier, the high court issued an interim order to the central government banning downloading of TikTok and restricting media from telecasting videos taken using the app.
The high court had passed the interim order citing inappropriate and pornographic content.
Tamil Nadu’s Information Technology Minister M. Manikandan said the state would write to the central government seeking a ban on TikTok in India.
The high court appointed leading lawyer Arvind Datar as an independent counsel to the court.
On an appeal by ByteDance, the Supreme Court asked the Madras High Court to decide on TikTok’s plea for interim relief by April 24, failing which the ban would stand lifted.
The Supreme Court refused to pass any order in the matter.
TikTok said it was committed to continuously enhancing its safety features and was grateful for the opportunity to serve users better.

1-16189-3-1.subevent: Venezuelan consumer prices rose 800 percent in 2016, according to preliminary central bank figures.
The economy contracted by 18.6 percent in 2016, the sharpest contraction in 13 years.
The extended slump in oil prices turned the OPEC nation’s once-prosperous oil-boom economy into one with rampant product shortages.
President Nicolas Maduro’s government blamed the situation on an “economic war” led by political adversaries with the help of the United States.
The central bank stopped releasing quarterly and monthly economic indicators.
The oil sector shrank 12.7 percent in 2016.
The non-oil sector shrank 19.5 percent in 2016.
A source said the figures could be changed in the process of approval by the central bank’s board of directors.
The central bank reported that in 2015 the economy contracted 5.7 percent and inflation reached 180.9 percent.
Maduro accused opposition-linked businesses of artificially creating economic problems.
Maduro said inflation is the result of speculative price-gouging by unscrupulous capitalists.
Maduro insisted workers are better off as a result of minimum wage increases in 2016 that totaled 454 percent.
Maduro said during a news conference this week that minimum wage increases are well above 2016 inflation.
Currency controls left businesses unable to obtain dollars, leading to stock shortages and idle factories.
Venezuelans last year began crossing into neighboring Brazil and Colombia to buy groceries.
Investor concern about Venezuela’s ability to service its foreign debt made its bonds among the highest-yielding emerging market securities.
Maduro dismissed rumors that the country or state oil company PDVSA could default, noting that the ruling Socialist Party has never missed a bond payment.

32-2285-2-1.subevent: A driver in Oakland commented on a billboard proclaiming Kawhi Leonard as "The King of the North" before Game 3 of the NBA Finals.
The Raptors took a 3-1 lead in the NBA Finals after winning Game 4 in Oakland, with many Warriors fans leaving early and the Raptors showing little emotion.
Kawhi Leonard recorded his 14th 30-point playoff game in Game 4, joining an elite group of players.
Steph Curry's best Finals performance came in a Game 3 loss, and Kevin Durant was cleared to practice on Sunday.
Nick Nurse called Game 4 critical and joked about needing three wins first.
The Raptors had won five of six matchups against the Warriors and 13 of 16 quarters in the series; FiveThirtyEight gave the Warriors an 11 percent chance to recover.
Steph Curry and Draymond Green expressed frustration after the loss, with Green saying "This sucks."
Nurse said the Raptors flipped a switch in Game 2 against Orlando after losing Game 1 to the Magic.
After losing Game 1 to the Magic, the Raptors won the next four games by large margins.
Leonard scored 39 points in Game 4 against the Sixers and made the Game 7 shot to win the series.
After losing the first two games to the Bucks, the Raptors won four straight, including a double-overtime Game 3; Nurse said the team wasn't upset.
The Raptors' starting lineup had logged only 161 regular-season minutes together before the playoffs.
After Game 4, Kyle Lowry took a selfie with a young Warriors fan.

9-21834-8-1.subevent: President Trump declares Sunday a National Day of Prayer after designating a national emergency.
Megachurches stream their Sunday services online, and Trump tweets that he is watching a service by Pastor Jentezen Franklin.
Trump's personal physician states he tested negative for the coronavirus.
Pastor Jentezen Franklin preaches a message titled 'Choose faith over fear' to an empty auditorium viewed by nearly 200,000, and thanks Trump while reading the National Day of Prayer proclamation.
Franklin says, 'The building and the seats are not the church, the people are the church.'
Greg Laurie's Harvest Fellowship sees over 230,000 online attendees, four times the normal number, and over 1,400 people commit to follow Jesus.
LifeBridge Community Church offers online services with curbside prayer, and lead pastor Kevin Foster says they want to spread a pandemic of hope.
Dr. Alveda King urges Americans, 'Don't panic. Pray,' and says she plans to attend service in person with precautions.

Smaller churches face hard decisions; at St. Philip AME Church in Atlanta, about 100 congregants attend, and Rev. William Watley says he will follow official directives, expresses faith, and urges hand washing.
Over 300 salvations are reported from Woodlands Church’s online services.
Roman Catholic bishops in Pennsylvania and Ohio dispense with the Mass attendance obligation, and Utah Bishop Oscar Solis announces a general dispensation and suggests praying at home.
Leaders of other faiths, including Orthodox Jewish rabbis and Episcopal and United Methodist bishops, take comparable measures.
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints halts all worship services worldwide.
The Vatican announces all public Masses in Italy are forbidden, and Pope Francis visits St. Mary Major Basilica to pray for the sick.
The article notes that over 6,470 people have died worldwide from the coronavirus, with at least 64 in the United States, and that most people recover in two to six weeks.

17-28164-3-1.subevent: Dale Coyne Racing announced a collaboration with Rick Ware Racing for a full-time entry and a part-time entry in the 2021 NTT IndyCar Series.
Coyne revealed that his second full-time entry, the #51 car, will be run in partnership with another team owner.
Rick Ware came onboard as co-entrant of the #51 and also the #52 entry, which will compete at the Indianapolis 500 and possibly other races.
Coyne said they were introduced to Rick Ware at the 2020 Indy 500 and have talked since, welcoming Rick Ware Racing into the Dale Coyne Racing family.
The primary sponsor of the #51 car will be announced in February, and the driver for that season-long entry is expected to be announced next week.
Ex-Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean is the favorite for the seat, although his participation in IndyCar's four oval races remains open to question.

If Grosjean chooses not to compete in the Texas double-header and the race at Gateway, a driver such as JR Hildebrand could be drafted in, but Hildebrand would not be available for the Indy 500 due to his ride with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing.
Ware stated that he met Dale Coyne last year through their Indy efforts, struck up a friendship, and thought about expanding into IndyCar, so the collaboration was an easy and logical step.
Rick Ware Racing currently fields four charters in the NASCAR Cup Series and has competed in various series since 2000.
The RWR Eurasia entry will compete in the LMP2 class at the Rolex 24 Hours at Daytona.

11-22309-3-t.subevent: Clergy groups in Muskogee are working to establish a fund to support a local mother who recently lost five of her children in a shooting.
Police say 25-year-old Jarron Deajon Pridgeon shot Brittany Anderson, five of her children, and his brother in a Muskogee home on Feb. 2.
Brittany Anderson is still recovering from the shooting, but the other victims died.
Muskogee Mayor Marlon Coleman announced plans for the fund Wednesday.
Mayor Coleman is asking the community to also support first responders.
Coleman plans to sign a proclamation in the next few days to establish the month of March as “Community Care Month for First Responders.”
Coleman says several first responders are getting therapy or counseling at this time because of the shooting.
Anderson is out of the hospital resting.
Funeral details for the children have yet to be announced.
Coleman plans to announce details on the fund to support the family soon.

0-4832-2-t.subevent: The Premier League suspended its 2019/20 season on 13 March 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic.
The Premier League worked with professional football in England, the Government, public agencies, and other stakeholders to resume the season.
Stage 1 of the 'Return to Training Protocol' allowed small-group training by players from 19 May 2020.
Stage 2 began on 27 May 2020, allowing clubs a resumption of contact training.
The 2019/20 season resumed on 17 June 2020 with matches taking place behind closed doors.
The League and clubs put in place strict medical protocols for the return to training, risk assessments, and regular testing programmes.
The 2020/21 season started with matches behind closed doors, apart from brief periods with limited fans in December 2020 and May 2021.
The 2021/22 season began with full stadiums, but the Premier League created matchday protocols to help keep everybody safe.
Players and club staff follow protocols for training and matchdays to protect their safety.

1-15241-6-4.subevent: Syrian firefighters and army helicopters battled forest fires for a seventh consecutive day in government-held areas.
Iran sent a firefighting plane carrying 40 tons of water to help fight fires in Latakia and Hama provinces.
State media published repeated images of billowing smoke above tree tops and charred vegetation.
Forestry official Hassan Fares said numerous fires have been put out, others brought under control, but fires continue to rage in some areas of Latakia.
The agriculture ministry said steep terrain was an obstacle to fire trucks reaching fire-hit areas quickly.
There was no immediate data for how large an area had been affected overall.
Hama governor Mohammed Al-Hazouri said the blaze had ravaged eight square kilometers of agricultural land in his province.
Summer fires are common in Syria, but residents said this year's are worse than usual.
Syria's war has killed more than 380,000 people, displaced millions from their homes, and decimated the country's economy.

1-14808-1-t.subevent: Businessman Zef Eisenberg died while attempting to break a British land speed record at Elvington Airfield.
He was driving a Porsche 911 Turbo S when he lost control and crashed.
North Yorkshire Police were called to the scene shortly after 4:30 p.m. the previous day.
Police confirmed the incident occurred during a British land speed record attempt and Eisenberg died at the scene.
Eisenberg had been involved in a dangerous crash at Elvington Airfield in 2016.
Ten years earlier, former Top Gear presenter Richard Hammond suffered a near-fatal accident at Elvington.
Motorsport UK said it was deeply saddened and would investigate the cause of the accident.
Motorsport UK described Eisenberg as a Guernsey-based businessman, television presenter, and much-loved member of the motorsport community.
Eisenberg leaves behind his partner Mirella D'Antonio and two children.
Over the past decade, Eisenberg amassed over 70 British, World, UKTA, ACU and Guinness speed records.
In May 2019, he received the Simms Medal for outstanding contribution to motoring innovation.
Eisenberg earned a world record in 2015 for reaching 225 mph on a turbine-powered motorbike.
He was attempting to break the British land speed record of 207.6 mph set by Tony Densham in 1970.

1-wiki-img/15302-2/15302-2-1.subevent: Armenia's forces hit Ganja, Azerbaijan's second-largest city, killing and injuring dozens of Azerbaijani civilians, less than a day after a humanitarian ceasefire between Yerevan and Baku came into effect.
Hikmat Hajiyev, senior aide to Azerbaijan's president, said Armenia is hiding behind the humanitarian ceasefire as part of its plan to attack Azerbaijani civilians.

Hajiyev wrote on Twitter that Ganja city came under missile attack by Armenia, destroying three residential buildings and killing seven civilians including women, and wounding 33 civilians including children.
The humanitarian ceasefire reached on Saturday called for the exchange of hostages and dead bodies through the mediation of the International Committee of the Red Cross.
Last night's attack on Ganja was the second of its kind throughout the ongoing clashes; the city was first hit on October 4.
Hajiyev added that the same attack was committed on Mingachevir city, which was hit by a Smerch heavy multiple rocket launcher received by Armenia during the humanitarian ceasefire period.

Hajiyev claimed that Atlantis Armenian Airlines transported the missiles and missile system onboard civilian aircraft to Armenia, violating the Chicago Convention and rules of the International Civil Aviation Organization.
Mingachevir is home to Azerbaijan's largest water dam, and a possible strike on the Mingachevir reservoir could be catastrophic for Azerbaijan and the entire region.

Officials at the National Center of Environmental Forecasting insisted that water from the dam could inundate a huge territory in Azerbaijan from the central part toward east up to Baku over 240 kilometers.
The latest clashes are the longest and fiercest fighting between Armenia and Azerbaijan since the countries reached a ceasefire in 1994.
The skirmishes along the Line of Contact erupted on September 27 after Armenia's troops began shelling military and civilian positions of Azerbaijan.
Azerbaijani forces took immediate counter-attack measures, and both sides have intensively deployed artillery, UAVs, mechanized forces, and infantry along the frontline.
As of Saturday, Armenian authorities confirmed the deaths of 405 servicemen, while the Defense Ministry of Azerbaijan said 2,300 servicemen of Armenia have been killed or wounded.
With the death toll of the recent attack on Ganja, the overall number of civilian casualties reached 40 in Azerbaijan along with over 200 injured residents.

The Armenia-Azerbaijan Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, which is over 30 years old, stems from the rise of anti-Azerbaijan sentiments in Armenia in 1988 due to Yerevan's illegal claims for Nagorno-Karabakh.

Following the Soviet Union's dissolution in 1991, Armenia launched a military campaign that lasted until a 1994 ceasefire, occupying 20 percent of Azerbaijan's territories and displacing one million ethnic Azerbaijanis.

6-19298-5-10.subevent: Kumbh Mela is the largest peaceful congregation of pilgrims on earth, during which participants bathe or take a dip in a sacred river.
Devotees believe that by bathing in the Ganges one is freed from sins, liberating her/him from the cycle of birth and death.
Millions of people reach the place without any invitation.
The congregation includes ascetics, saints, sadhus, aspirants-kalpavasis, and visitors.
The festival is held at Allahabad, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nasik every four years by rotation and is attended by millions of people irrespective of caste, creed, or gender.
Its primary bearers belong to akhadas and ashrams, religious organizations, or are individuals living on alms.
Kumbh Mela plays a central spiritual role in the country, exerting a mesmeric influence on ordinary Indians.
The event encapsulates the science of astronomy, astrology, spirituality, ritualistic traditions, and social and cultural customs and practices, making it extremely rich in knowledge.
As it is held in four different cities in India, it involves different social and cultural activities, making this a culturally diverse festival.
Knowledge and skills related to the tradition are transmitted through ancient religious manuscripts, oral traditions, historical travelogues, and texts produced by eminent historians.
The teacher-student relationship of the sadhus in the ashrams and akhadas remains the most important method of imparting and safeguarding knowledge and skills relating to Kumbh Mela.

5-5883-1-1.subevent: The European Space Agency is starting a regular series of small science missions.
The first winning 'S-Class' idea will receive 50 million euros and be readied for launch in 2017.
This departure contrasts with ESA's usual spending of hundreds of millions on flagship probes and telescopes.
ESA hopes to encourage young scientists and research teams from smaller member states.
Prof Mark McCaughrean stated the program can train people and give smaller states opportunities to lead missions.
Interested parties must submit expressions of interest by 23 March, followed by a defined proposal in June.
A selection of the best ideas will be chosen for study in November, with a winner selected 12 months later.
There is no directive on S-Class mission content, except it must fit within ESA's 'Cosmic Vision'.
National governments of winning scientists will likely fund instrument development in addition to ESA's 50 million euros.
The 'fast and small' philosophy likely excludes highly complex projects like deep-space probes or Mars landers.
More realistic mission concepts include compact space telescopes or fundamental physics experiments in Earth orbit.
The Lares spacecraft, launched in February on ESA's Vega rocket, is an example of a small mission.
Lares is a 37cm-diameter sphere with 92 reflectors used for laser ranging to study frame-dragging in general relativity.
Another example is ESA's Proba-2 satellite, which has an imager called Swap taking scientifically useful pictures of the Sun.
Swap tracked the solar storm that hurled billions of tonnes of plasma at Earth last week.
ESA is about to select its next large, or 'L-Class', mission from three competing ideas.
The competing ideas are a big X-ray telescope, a probe to Jupiter and its moons, and a general relativity experiment to detect gravitational waves.
The cost of the winning L-Class concept is likely around a billion euros.

26-13936-2-1.subevent: Millions of students, workers and scientists came together at the global climate strikes last week.
Over 7.6 million people held demonstrations on streets and squares.
The 350 Movement said this was almost equal to the 2003 anti-Iraq war protest, making it one of the biggest global demonstrations in history.
More than 6,100 events were held in 185 countries, with support from 73 Trade Unions, 820 civil society organizations, 3,000 companies and 8,500 websites.
Celebrities such as Leonardo DiCaprio, Keith Richards, Mick Jagger and Chris Hemsworth supported the strike on social media.
Italy, Germany, Canada, the U.S., and Spain were the five countries where most people attended the global climate strike.
Young climate activists gave powerful speeches to the authorities.
Major multinational oil company CEOs met with government representatives and diplomats in a lobbying effort on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly session in New York.
The movement stressed the importance of meeting the Paris Agreement goals and cutting global emissions of greenhouse gases.
The movement criticized big fossil fuel companies.
The statement concluded that big fossil fuel companies keep profiting from coal, oil and gas while the planet heats up and entire communities lose their lives and livelihoods.

0-4325-2-1.subevent: The opioid crisis is worsening due to new drugs like fentanyl.
A photograph shows a lethal dose of heroin (30 mg) and a lethal dose of fentanyl (3 mg).
Fentanyl is up to 100 times more potent than morphine and many times more potent than heroin.
Drug users generally don't know when their heroin is laced with fentanyl and may inadvertently take a deadly dose.
Dealers' measuring equipment is not fine-tuned enough to avoid overdose levels when adding fentanyl.
Street fentanyl is made in clandestine labs, is less pure, and its effects are more unpredictable.
Heroin and fentanyl look identical, and users do not know what they are taking, as stated by Tim Pifer.
New Hampshire had 439 drug overdoses in 2015, with about 70% of opioid-related deaths involving fentanyl.
The state has seen 200 deadly opioid overdoses so far this year, according to Pifer.
Fentanyl was originally used as an anesthetic and later for pain relief.
With trained professionals and laboratory-grade equipment, fentanyl has a wide therapeutic index.
The strength difference between heroin and fentanyl arises from fentanyl binding faster and tighter to the mu opioid receptor in the brain.

3-17502-3-t.subevent: The Portuguese Episcopal Conference announced on Jan. 21 that public Masses would be suspended from Jan. 23 due to the extreme gravity of the coronavirus crisis.
The bishops said it was a moral imperative to take maximum sanitary precautions to avoid contagion and contribute to overcoming the situation.
Portugal is experiencing a surge in COVID-19 deaths, with 609,000 cases and 9,920 deaths as of Jan. 22.
This is the second time the bishops have suspended public worship, the first being in March 2020 with restrictions eased at the end of May.
The suspension includes public Masses, catechesis, and other pastoral activities requiring gatherings, with priests asked to offer livestreamed Masses.
Earlier in January, the bishops called for the suspension or postponement of baptisms, confirmations, and marriages.
Funerals may be celebrated according to norms from May 2020 requiring social distance.
A Lenten retreat for the bishops scheduled for Feb. 22-26 has been canceled.
The Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima will broadcast three Masses and two rosary prayers daily during the suspension.
The broadcasts will occur at 11 a.m., 12:30 p.m., and 3 p.m. for Masses, and 6:30 p.m. and 9:30 p.m. for the rosary.
Shrine rector Fr. Carlos Cabecinhas said that following on television is not the same as being physically present but is the only possible way to participate now.

26-14496-4-1.subevent: Both Toyota TS050 Hybrids initially hover around the 3m21s mark.
Sebastien Buemi fires off a lap of 3m19.719s in the #8 car just before the two-hour mark.
Buemi’s time is nine tenths clear of the #7 sister car, which is second-fastest courtesy of Mike Conway's late 3m20.611s.
Nathanael Berthon puts the #3 Rebellion R-13 in third, 3.456s removed from Buemi’s benchmark.
The lone #4 ByKolles entry is fourth in class, but slower than the leading LMP2 car, Tom Dillmann clocking a 3m27.304s at the start of the session.
Rebellion’s #1 car is stuck in the garage for most of the session to complete an engine change.
In LMP2, reigning FIA Formula 2 champion Nyck de Vries sets a benchmark of 3m27.884s in the first hour in the #29 Racing Team Nederland Oreca 07.
It takes until the final hour for the competition to catch up to the Dutchman, Will Stevens clocking a 3m28.011s in the #37 Jackie Chan DC Racing Oreca.
De Vries then puts the Dutch team further out in front with a 3m27.185s in the yellow machine.
Formula E champion Antonio Felix da Costa is third in the #38 JOTA Sport Oreca, a further five tenths back from Stevens.

Aston Martin looks set to continue its clean sweep in GTE Pro until Michael Christensen overhauls Alex Lynn’s time to go fastest in the #92 Porsche RSR-19, setting a time of 3m52.783s in the final 20 minutes of the session, bettering Lynn’s benchmark in the #97 Aston Martin Vantage by more than half a second.
Gianmaria Bruni is third in the #91 Porsche, followed by Toni Vilander in the #63 WeatherTech Racing Ferrari and James Calado in the #51 AF Corse Ferrari.

In GTE Am the #98 Aston long remains on top by virtue of Augusto Farfus’ early laptime of 3m55.167s, until Come Ledogar betters the Brazilian’s time with just 10 minutes to go in the #61 Luzich Ferrari.
Ledogar is then overhauled himself by Matt Campbell in the #77 Dempsey Proton Porsche, who lowers the benchmark to 3m53.961s, which is the fifth-fastest time of any GTE car.
The session is red flagged twice for heavy crashes, each involving an IDEC Sport LMP2 car.
Just before the one-hour mark Paul Lafargue hits the barriers coming out of the second chicane in the #28 IDEC Sport Oreca.

An hour later, teammate Dwight Merriman crashes heavily coming out of the Porsche Curves in the #17 sister car, meaning the French team is facing an uphill battle to get ready for Thursday afternoon’s first 45-minute qualifying session.
The fastest six cars in each class from that session will progress to Friday’s Hyperpole shootout.

1-15227-1-1.subevent: Pakistan blocked TikTok after the company failed to fully comply with instructions to develop an effective mechanism to control unlawful content.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority said it took the step after receiving complaints against immoral and indecent content on the platform.
The PTA said it issued a final notice and gave TikTok considerable time to respond and comply with instructions and guidelines.
TikTok failed to fully comply with the PTA's instructions, leading to the ban.
Shortly after the ban, the TikTok app began to show a blank interface with no text or images loading.
The PTA left the door open for a return of TikTok, saying it is open for engagement and would review its decision if TikTok develops a content moderation mechanism.
TikTok has been the target of several complaints and court petitions calling for its ban in Pakistan, and in July the PTA issued a final warning to remove obscene and immoral content.
Pakistani TikTok celebrity Hareem Shah said the government's reasons for the ban were unfounded.
She said the talk of TikTok being a platform for indecent/immoral content is completely unfounded.
She added that such government actions could lead to further encroachment on creative liberties in the country.
She said TikTok is a very good app for entertainment and showcases the talent of Pakistani youth.
TikTok is the third-most downloaded app over the past year after WhatsApp and Facebook and has been downloaded almost 39 million times in Pakistan.
TikTok was earlier banned by India and the United States for violating guidelines.

1-15874-5-1.subevent: A relocatable lander called Dragonfly could explore the hazy skies of Saturn's moon Titan.
Dragonfly could investigate potentially habitable sites on Titan where methane and ethane fall from the sky and flow as rivers and lakes.
Dragonfly would take advantage of Titan's low gravity and thick atmosphere to visit multiple sites over several years, moving and recharging between brief flights.
Principal investigator Elizabeth Turtle said Titan is a rich place to explore in situ and that the environment hands us the way to explore it.
Turtle, a planetary scientist at Johns Hopkins Applied Research Laboratory, is leading the team proposing an in-depth exploration of Titan as part of NASA's New Frontiers program.
Turtle presented the Dragonfly concept at the Lunar and Planetary Sciences Conference in The Woodlands, Texas.
On Titan, flowing methane and ethane rivers and seas provide an opportunity to explore the chemistry that could lead to the rise of life.
The thick atmosphere makes the mission possible.
Turtle said the atmosphere gives us the ability to travel on Titan.

8-6386-5-t.subevent: A video published Thursday appeared to show how the Houston Astros allegedly used whistles to tip pitches to batters during the 2017 World Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The video claimed that the Astros used two different whistling noises to signal to batters that a fastball or a breaking ball was about to be pitched.
The video broke down at-bats from Josh Reddick, George Springer, Evan Gattis, Yuli Gurriel, and Jose Altuve during the World Series.

The Astros came under scrutiny after former Astros pitcher Mike Fiers and other unnamed sources revealed to The Athletic that the team used a sophisticated system to steal signs using a camera in centerfield connected to a monitor in the clubhouse.
Two sources told The Athletic that the sign-stealing extended into the postseason in 2017, but another source denied it went on that long.

A 2017 DVD commemorating the Astros' first World Series championship showed a table, chairs, and a TV in the clubhouse which appeared to be the area where a team employee would alert batters to an upcoming pitch.
Twitter user Jomboy again brought to light the team’s alleged cheating setup using video from the team’s championship DVD.
MLB commissioner Rob Manfred said Thursday an investigation was underway encompassing not only 2017 but also 2018 and 2019.
Manfred said the Astros were the only team being investigated for now.
Astros owner Jim Crane declined to comment on the allegations when he was seen Wednesday.

0-4930-1-3.subevent: A police Eurocopter EC135 T2 helicopter crashed through the roof of the Clutha Vaults pub in Glasgow city centre at around 10.25pm.
The helicopter was carrying two police officers and a civilian pilot, and a band was playing inside the bar at the time of the crash.
Eyewitnesses reported seeing badly injured people at the scene.
By Saturday morning, police confirmed that 32 people had been taken to hospitals and rescue crews were continuing to recover others.
Scotland's first minister Alex Salmond tweeted that fatalities were likely and confirmed the helicopter was a police aircraft.
Police Scotland declared a major incident and established cordons to allow the rescue operation.
Assistant Chief Officer Lewis Ramsay said firefighters were treating the incident as a rescue operation, with 125 firefighters on scene stabilizing the building.
Labour MP Jim Murphy described how members of the public formed a human chain to help people out of the pub.
Witness Wesley McEwan, who was inside the bar, described hearing an explosion and seeing people trapped under the helicopter.
Witness Grace MacLean described hearing a whoosh noise and seeing the roof come down as people screamed.
Journalist Gordon Smart reported seeing the helicopter falling from the sky like a stone without an explosion.
Deputy Chief Constable Rose Fitzpatrick delivered a statement confirming the details and that a joint investigation with the Air Accident Investigation Branch had begun.

0-4551-2-t.subevent: The Turkish judiciary attempted to close down the governing Justice and Development Party (AKP).
Current political tensions in Turkey date back further than the recent closure attempt.
The tensions are linked to broader issues of secularism versus Islamism.
The situation may have implications for Turkey's status as an EU accession candidate.
The outcome of the court ruling will signal the beginning of a new era in Turkish politics.
The only way out of the political impasse is the adoption of a conciliatory attitude by all parties.

The conciliatory attitude seems a remote possibility due to the governing party's questioned democratic credentials, the opposition's lack of credible alternative policy, and the judiciary's entrenched beliefs.

13-wiki-img/25021-4/25021-4-1.subevent: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said measures have been taken to compensate the victims of the Sohag train collision and their families, as well as precautions to avoid such accidents.

Solidarity Minister Nevine el-Kabbag said President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi demanded that compensations are dispensed promptly, as well as providing medical, psychological and social care for the victims.

Kabbag said the family of a victim killed in the accident is entitled to L.E. 100,000, and a victim who has incurred a disability will be compensated commensurately with the injury from L.E. 100,000 to L.E. 40,000, and a lifetime pension will be available for the victims.
Kabbag said L.E. 20,000 have already been available for the families of the deceased since Saturday as part of prompt compensation, and L.E. 5,000-10,000 for the injured.
Kabbag said Al-Azhar and NGOs have expressed willingness to help with the social assistance of the victims and their families in terms of education, work and psychological welfare.
Minister of Health Hala Zayed said the death toll reported at the time of the accident was not accurate because people in post-concussion coma were initially reported dead.
Zayed said 20 people were in such coma.
Zayed said the latest death toll stands at 19 after it was first reported to be more than 30.
Zayed said the first ambulance arrived at the scene five minutes after the accident.
Zayed praised the locals for helping emergency crews.

3-18343-1-t.subevent: Pitt's men's basketball and football programs were placed on three years' probation.
Former basketball coach Kevin Stallings received a three-year show-cause order.
Stallings instructed and allowed three non-coaching staff members to perform coaching duties, exceeding the number of permissible coaches.
Pitt self-reported the violation prior to the NCAA launching its investigation.
Athletic director Heather Lyke released a statement affirming Pitt's commitment to integrity and NCAA rules compliance.
Stallings developed an alert system to ensure the non-permissible coaches would not get caught.
Stallings ordered the deletion of video to prevent Pitt administration from confirming the violations.
Despite warnings from administrators, Stallings did not cease the violations and failed to promote an atmosphere of compliance.
Under the show-cause order, if Stallings is hired by a member school within three years, he must be suspended from 30% of the first season.
Pitt's former director of basketball operations produced personalized recruiting videos for 12 prospects and later refused to participate in an enforcement interview.
Football coach Pat Narduzzi was present at a practice when three former quality control staff members performed coaching duties, exceeding the number of permissible coaches.
The violation went undetected in part because the football program used a system to play music when outside parties were present, triggering quality control staff to stay clear of student-athletes.
Narduzzi received a show-cause order that will withhold him from two days of team practice in August.
Narduzzi issued a statement accepting responsibility and committing to following NCAA rules.
Pitt received a $5,000 fine from the men's basketball and football budgets and a three-year show-cause order for the former director of basketball operations.

The men's basketball program will have a reduction of one countable coach for 16 hours of regular practice in 2019-20, and the football program will have a reduction of one countable coach for four days of practice and removal of two quality control staff from practice for three days.

1-16165-3-2.subevent: The Australian Grand Prix has been called off because of coronavirus.
The first McLaren team member was identified as having the coronavirus on Thursday evening.
The FIA and Formula 1 issued a joint statement with the Australian Grand Prix Corporation announcing the cancellation of all Formula 1 activity for the Australian Grand Prix.
Mercedes announced that they would be withdrawing from the event before the cancellation.
Ferrari issued a statement supporting the decision to cancel the race.
Organisers initially claimed the event would go on as planned and hospitality staff were told to attend.
Fans arriving were refused entry to the track with little information as to why.
Victoria's state premier Daniel Andrews said that if the race was to be held, it would have to take place behind closed doors.
At least two drivers, Kimi Raikkonen and Sebastian Vettel, had already flown home before the cancellation.
Lewis Hamilton expressed concern that the race was putting lives in danger with 300,000 fans expected.
McLaren confirmed that a member of their team had tested positive for coronavirus.
The cancellation of the Australian Grand Prix put the upcoming Bahrain and Vietnam Grands Prix under major threat.

9-20780-1-1.subevent: Google suspended the Parler social networking app from its Play Store until it adds robust content moderation.
Twitter permanently suspended the US president's account over the risk of further incitement to violence.
Apple gave Parler 24 hours to submit a detailed moderation plan.
Plans for the protests that ended in the storming of the Capitol were widely shared on Parler.
Parler CEO John Matze said in posts on his service that Apple was applying standards to Parler that it did not apply to itself and the companies were attacking civil liberties.
Matze said in a text message to Reuters: 'Coordinating riots, violence and rebellions has no place on social media.'

Google cited its policy against apps that promote violence and gave examples from Parler, including a post that began 'How do we take back our country? About 20 or so coordinated hits' and another promoting a 'Million Militia March'.
Google said in a statement that it requires apps to implement robust moderation for egregious content and that it was suspending Parler's listing until it addresses these issues.
Apple cited participants of the mob storming the US Capitol building in a letter from its App Store review team to Parler.
Apple said in the letter that content threatening the well-being of others or inciting violence has never been acceptable on the App Store.
Apple gave Parler 24 hours to remove all objectionable content and submit a written plan to moderate and filter content.
Matze founded Parler in 2018 as a 'free-speech driven' alternative to mainstream platforms and began courting right-leaning users.
Users who joined Parler include commentator Candace Owens, Trump's lawyer Rudy Giuliani, and rightwing activist Laura Loomer.
Conservative activist Rebekah Mercer confirmed that she and her family have provided funding to Parler.

0-4403-2-2.subevent: French Interior Minister Christophe Castaner said signs of Islamist radicalisation should trigger an 'automatic alert' and deplored 'failings' that allowed Mickaël Harpon to kill four police colleagues.
Mickaël Harpon was shot dead on Thursday after stabbing colleagues at the Paris police headquarters.
Castaner said police should have investigated Harpon's suspicious behaviour in 2015, but nobody raised any formal concerns.
Castaner said investigators only learnt on Friday that in 2015 some of Harpon's colleagues had spoken about his praise for the jihadist attack on Charlie Hebdo.
Police colleagues had also commented on Harpon's changed behaviour towards women, but no concerns were formally reported.
Castaner said that if a signal had appeared perhaps they could have prevented the attack.
About 20 officers in the French security services have been taken off duty because of suspected Islamist radicalisation.
Castaner brushed off calls for his resignation and pledged to 'tighten the net' to pick up suspicious signs.
Harpon, a 45-year-old IT expert, had been working in the police intelligence unit since 2003 and had contact with members of the Salafist movement.
On Thursday morning, shortly before his attack, Harpon exchanged 33 text messages with his wife including religious phrases such as 'Allahu akbar'.
Harpon's wife was questioned by police but released; she reportedly told police that he had been incoherent and had heard voices the night before.
Anti-terror investigators took over the inquiry on Friday, which was initially regarded as a criminal matter.
Harpon was shot dead on Thursday by a junior police officer after he attacked colleagues in several offices.
Investigators established that Harpon left the building at lunchtime and bought two knives half an hour before launching his attack.

He stabbed three people inside two offices and two women on a stairway, then was shot dead in the courtyard; three men and one woman were killed, one person was seriously injured, and he slit the throat of one victim.

5-6042-3-t.subevent: Patriarch Kirill noted the work to overcome schisms in Universal Orthodoxy generated by the anti-canonical invasion of the Patriarch of Constantinople into Ukraine.
Patriarch Kirill said that Patriarch Bartholomew was probably guided not by his own reason or will.
Patriarch Kirill rejected allegations that the Patriarch of Constantinople could not act otherwise due to external pressure, citing the Russian Church's experience under an atheistic state.
Patriarch Kirill mentioned that Constantinople has had martyrs and confessors, and was a stronghold of Orthodoxy.
Patriarch Kirill stated that Patriarch Bartholomew has lapsed into schism because he took communion with schismatics and recognized self-ordained clergy.
Patriarch Kirill stressed that while aware of their truth, they should seek pastorally and humanly to overcome the difficult time in inter-Orthodox relations.

35-5391-7-1.subevent: NATO took the lead of the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) in Afghanistan on 11 August 2003.
